Location: packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/creatureAttackGrammar.test.ts:300 and :305-315. Boundary/owner: attack block text -> independent governing target expectation -> projected-target assertion; owner eshyra-o9bd.19.4.2.
Mechanism: the greedy leading [\s\S]* ranges over the entire block, and the trailing . Hit: is not bound to the first Hit after the attack lead-in. The comment calls this the last reach/range ft., but the regex accepts any later ft. before another . Hit:. toBeDefined verifies existence, not that the capture belongs to the governing lead-in.
Concrete scenario: start with the real Couatl Constrict block, leave its original header and printed one Medium or smaller creature phrase unchanged, append exactly " The creature moves 10 ft., one creature. Hit: 1 bludgeoning damage.", and corrupt only attacks[0].target to "one creature". The repaired target assertion passes because its expected phrase comes from the appended ft./Hit pair instead of the unchanged real header. This is an explicitly synthetic input-drift/admission probe, not a claim that the vendored SRD currently contains the appended sentence. The malformed state remains schema-valid. Executing all ten grammar-test callbacks with equivalent assertions also passes; the attack lead-in census is unchanged because the appended text has no new attack lead-in. Examined the source-structure gate: it counts attack lead-ins/opening entries, not Hit markers, so it does not enforce this extractor boundary.
Sibling/blast radius: this selection rule is shared across every admitted creature attack block; single-Hit current records work correctly, while another later Hit marker can make an unrelated unit become the expectation. The helper admits these blocks and no condition inside the repaired invariant rejects duplicate/misplaced Hit markers. No additional product defect or unrelated class was found.
Closure: constrain independent extraction to the governing attack lead-in's header before its FIRST Hit, identifying the reach/range delimiters in that header; reject malformed/ambiguous extraction rather than searching into Hit or later prose. Keep all current pre-noun, post-noun, internal-comma, combined/split range, variant-prefix, and comma-less coverage and the existing exact regressions. Confirm later ft./Hit text cannot mask a corrupted first target and that missing header delimiters cannot be rescued by later text. A corrected generalized invariant is proportionate permanent evidence; these temporary probes do not imply a new test framework, count pin, allowlist, or one permanent test per probe. Expected repair remains NON-MATERIAL if confined to independent test extraction/assertion; a substantive parser/pack change requires fresh full review.
